data.name: Legal_Privacy_Intro
data.value: Hi — I'm Adrian, and I built CircleTools for my own family. I care about your data the way I care about mine, so I keep as little of it as possible. Every app works offline with no account at all; if you'd like to sync across your devices, you can create one. Here's exactly what happens to your data when you do, in plain language. (For the record, this follows Swiss data-protection law — the revDSG — and the EU's GDPR where it applies.)

data.name: Legal_Privacy_ControllerBody
data.value: It's just me — Adrian Moll, a software engineer building CircleTools (circletools.ch) in my free time. If you ever have a question about your data, write to me at info@circletools.ch and I'll answer.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_DataBody
data.value: If you create an account, I store your email address, a display name you pick, your language, a one-way scramble of your password, and — if you use a passkey — its public part. To make shared groups and circles work, I store what you put in them: the names, wishlists, event details and the pairings a draw produces. I deliberately don't ask for your birthday, your address, your phone number or any payment details. And email addresses used only to match invitations are stored scrambled, never in plain text.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_LocalFirstHeading
data.value: Without an account, nothing leaves your device

data.name: Legal_Privacy_LocalFirstBody
data.value: If you skip the account, everything you create stays on your own device — in your browser, or in a file on your phone — and never reaches me. The one exception is sharing a group by link: that uploads the group so the people you share it with can open it, and you choose to do that.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_LegalBasisHeading
data.value: Why I'm allowed to handle it

data.name: Legal_Privacy_LegalBasisBody
data.value: I use your account and content to give you the app you asked for. Extras like reminder emails happen only if you say yes, and you can change your mind at any time. Keeping the app secure and free of abuse is the one thing I do simply because I have to.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_ProcessorsHeading
data.value: Where it lives, and who helps run it

data.name: Legal_Privacy_ProcessorsBody
data.value: Your account and synced data sit on servers at Infomaniak in Geneva, Switzerland. The few emails the app sends — confirming your address, resetting your password, invitations — go through Brevo, a provider in the EU. Apart from those emails, your data stays in Switzerland, and these companies only ever act on my instructions.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_RetentionBody
data.value: An account you start but never confirm is cleaned up after 30 days. Sign-in tokens roll over on a 30-day window and are dropped when you reset your password or delete your account. An invitation disappears the moment it's accepted, declined or expires. And when you delete your account, it's gone from the live service right away, for good — the only trace that lingers is in the encrypted backups I keep for disaster recovery, which a deleted account drops out of within a few months as they roll over.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_RightsBody
data.value: You can see, correct, download and delete your data whenever you like — export and delete are right there in the app under your account, with no request and no waiting. If something's on your mind, just email me at info@circletools.ch. And if you ever feel I've mishandled your data, you're free to raise it with the Swiss Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) or your local authority.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_CookiesBody
data.value: I only use the local storage the app needs to work — your session and your preferences. No advertising cookies, no third-party trackers, no profiling. That's just not my thing.

data.name: Legal_Privacy_ChangesBody
data.value: If the app grows and this needs updating, I'll update it right here — the date at the top always shows the current version, and I'll flag anything important inside the app.

data.name: Legal_Imprint_OperatorBody
data.value: CircleTools is run by me, Adrian Moll (circletools.ch). The best way to reach me is info@circletools.ch.

data.name: Legal_Imprint_HostingBody
data.value: The app runs on servers at Infomaniak in Geneva, Switzerland.

data.name: Legal_Imprint_DisclaimerBody
data.value: I build this with care, but it's a free personal project — I can't promise it's always perfect or always available, and, as far as the law allows, I can't take on liability for problems that come from using it. Links to other sites are theirs, not mine, so their content is their responsibility.

data.name: Legal_Delete_Intro
data.value: This is where you remove your data from Secret Santa and the other CircleTools apps I build — I'm Adrian Moll, and CircleTools is mine. Your data is yours, and leaving is easy. Here's how to remove it — whether that's your whole account, a single thing inside it, or something kept only on your device.

data.name: Legal_Delete_InAppBody
data.value: Sign in, open the account menu in the top-right corner, and go to your account settings. Choose "Delete account" and confirm. It happens straight away and for good: your profile, your circle memberships, the invitations you sent and the groups you own are all removed, with no way back.

data.name: Legal_Delete_PartialHeading
data.value: Deleting some things without deleting your account

data.name: Legal_Delete_PartialBody
data.value: You don't have to leave to tidy up. While you're signed in, you can delete individual things and keep your account: on the Groups screen, open a group's menu and choose "Delete" to remove the group and everything in it; inside a group, open an event's menu and choose "Remove" to delete just that event; on a group's Members list, open a member's menu and choose "Remove" to delete that person and their entries; and under My wishlists, delete single items or a whole list. Each of these takes effect on my servers right away while you're signed in. If you can't find the option for something, email me at info@circletools.ch and I'll sort it out.

data.name: Legal_Delete_WhatBody
data.value: Everything tied to your account goes. People you added to a circle as managed profiles stay, because they belong to the circle rather than to you, and the other members still count on them. A group you shared by link can be handed over to or kept by the others in it — you decide what happens to it as you delete.

data.name: Legal_Delete_RetentionBody
data.value: When you delete your account or a single thing, it's gone from the live service straight away — I can't get it back, and neither can you. The one exception is my encrypted backups, which I keep only for disaster recovery: deleted data can sit in an older backup for up to about six months before it rolls off for good, and I never restore a backup to bring deleted data back, only to recover from a real outage.

data.name: Legal_Delete_LocalHeading
data.value: Data kept only on your device

data.name: Legal_Delete_LocalBody
data.value: If you use an app without an account, its data lives only on your device. Remove it by deleting the group or event in the app, or by clearing the app's site data in your browser or its settings. That data never reached me, so there's nothing on my side to delete.

data.name: Legal_Delete_ContactBody
data.value: If you can't get into your account to delete it, email me at info@circletools.ch and I'll help you out.

data.name: Legal_Imprint_AboutBody
data.value: I'm a software engineer, and I built CircleTools in my free time. It started as a Secret-Santa app for my own family — I couldn't find one that did what we needed — and slowly grew into a small set of tools for families and groups of friends. I share it freely, and I hope it makes your get-togethers a little easier.
